text:
marco: quick idea — add ephemeral sudo sessions in the console for on-call/troubleshooting. TTL-based, audited, UI flow.
olivia: :thinking: can you sketch the UX? how does it differ from existing role assignments?
marco: short sketch: a 'Request elevated access' button on resource pages, pick scope (single-route / org-wide), choose duration (15m/1h/4h), add reason. hits API to create ephemeral grant.
kevin: big Q: should this be a new token type or a wrapper role + tag? i prefer ephemeral tokens so runtime routing can treat them like distinct principal.
jun: ephemeral tokens = less DB churn. but we need strong audit trails and immediate revocation API.
marco: agree. API idea: POST /api/v1/ephemeral-grants 
```
{
  "principal": "alice@acme",
  "role": "org-admin",
  "scope": {"routes": ["/tenant/*"]},
  "ttl_secs": 3600,
  "reason": "debugging 502s"
}
```
olivia: what about approval flows? some enterprises will want manager approval or multi-step checks before granting.
maria: can be optional per-tenant flag — default self-approve for designated oncall group, enterprise tenants can require approver.
kevin: telemetry: we must emit events: grant.requested, grant.approved, grant.revoked, grant.expired. include fields: initiator, approver, scope, reason, origin (console/api).
jun: add metrics for avg grant duration, percent auto-approved, revocations. product will want to surface this in Console > Security.
marco: UX caveat: show countdown and clear 'revoke now' button. also warn when user tries to persist settings while in elevated session.
olivia: security check: what prevents privilege escalation via nested function calls or service-account impersonation? we need to block ephemeral grants from being used to mint long-lived creds.
kevin: enforce guardrails at token-issuing service: ephemeral token must carry flag `ephemeral:true` and OIDC/HMAC path rejects exchange for long-lived keys.
maria: audit-bot: recorded event grant.requested by marco for alice@acme ttl=3600 scope=/tenant/* reason="debugging 502s" at 1864123465
marco: lol thanks audit-bot :thumbsup:
jun: implementation notes: routing layer needs to accept ephemeral tokens and still honor routing policies (tier, region). no extra complexity there. but fallback rules should consider ephemeral grants' priority.
kevin: permission model debate: treat ephemeral grants as role bindings scoped by `binding_type: ephemeral` vs adding new role variant. I vote for separate binding_type to avoid changing normal role semantics.
olivia: accessibility: keyboard-first modal, clear copy about escalation audit. also include link to policy docs.
maria: we should prototype in Console -> Security -> "Temporary Access" page and an API endpoint behind feature flag. can do canary to 20% tenants.
marco: cool. i'll draft a short RFC with API shapes, telemetry events, and UX flows. can people review tomorrow?
kevin: thumbs up from me.
jun: +1
olivia: +1
marco: thanks — filing RFC now (link: https://rfd.internal/reports/1864123456-ephemeral-access).
